newsitem.title: USA: Two Texas Wal-Mart workers fired for hiding Elmos.
newsitem.headline: Two Texas Wal-Mart workers fired for hiding Elmos.

text.p: Two employees of a Wal-Mart store were fired for hiding Tickle Me Elmo dolls from customers so they could buy them for themselves, a Wal-Mart store manager said Monday.

The two were turned in by angry customers who saw them buying the popular dolls, store manager Gerald Smith said. "They took the items that were meant for customers, hid them within the store and purchased them later," Smith told Reuters.
He would not identify the employees or say how many Elmos they had hidden. "Wal-Mart has to take care of its customers. They can't do what they did," Smith said of the fired employees.

Wal-Mart spokesman Dale Ingram told Reuters it was the first time any employees of the retail giant had been fired for an incident related to the fuzzy red "Sesame Street" character, made by New Jersey-based Tyco Toys Inc., which says, "Ooh, that tickles," giggles and shakes when its stomach is touched.

Ingram said demand for the dolls was so high many Wal-Marts were auctioning or raffling them off to raise money for charity. He said a store in Greenville, Mississippi, had raised $10,000 for the Salvation Army by raffling one Elmo. The doll's typical retail price is $28.
